body:
# Design authoring basis

The user authorized Design after independent Proposal Review. Design, System and the scoped Workflow amendment are the exact authored package. The existing architecture/spec skills supplied technical and behavioral authorship under the adopted living-model profile. Design DES-DEC-01–05 and System SYS-DEC-01–03 own the engineering rationale; their maps identify all architecture-method R1–R124, both method ADRs, the exact mixed-system boundary and retained owners. Delivery owns concrete edit/proof allocation. No public skill, installer, governing consumer or release is changed in this authoring step.

## Applicability and handoff

The proposal and its independent review remain unchanged. Workflow has a new subject identity: earlier Design/Code/Verify assessments must not be reused as approval of this convention transfer. Prior records and identities remain unchanged, and no old approval is restored or retargeted. The new package has no Design approval; independent Design Review must assess all three subjects and relevant relationships before planning relies on it.

Review and Closeout, Test, Record Format and CLI remain unchanged policy/mechanical dependencies. Earlier Workflow retirement exclusions describe the earlier initiative, not this later approved direction. Two already-broken historical proposal links in Workflow were converted to explicit unavailable-source citations, with no historical artifact reconstruction or current-authority claim.

Current authority changes only at coordinated adoption. Public spec/architecture entrypoints are withdrawn together; the Design contract specifies safe installer rejection with operator-controlled cleanup, no automatic deletion and no new record schema. Unmigrated-source work remains supported under its declared contract. Remaining consolidation has named ownership intent; Delivery/Route must assign durable follow-up before adoption closeout.

Structural/prose/readability and link/enumeration checks passed. The 134 readability warnings remain non-blocking. No target-agent correctness, generated-package behavior, runtime/token savings, implementation or final Verify is claimed. Independent Design Review is next; no automatic continuation is armed.

decisions.rationale: User corrections des-review-f2/f3/f4: unconditional manual removal changed the locked tree before drift checks. DES-DEC-04 now selects installer-owned TNI-DES-01–06 narrowly authorized managed replacement under existing --write-state, original-basis verification, backup, neighbor/state protection, exclusive/unchanged write basis and rollback/interruption recovery; unmanaged cleanup remains separate. This is a required adopting extension of the observed workflow-to-route mechanism, not a claim it already supports design. Installation remains unmigrated; target-native-init registry identity denotes the affected retained responsibility, not a new consolidated model. Its substantive amendment adopts boundary-first-v1 scoped to TNI-DES IDs, preserving the original body and historical approval meaning. Named complete conditional feature/core/legacy-technical resources and installed assets close portable legacy authoring; customer authority remains separate. Workflow names Design mapping owner and itself coordination consumer. Package membership references include the installer amendment. Earlier shared narrative is historical first-draft evidence; this decision and exact subjects describe the correction. Prior approvals are not retargeted; original reporter owns finding disposition. No implementation, installation, release or adoption performed. Subsequent reporter finding f5 corrected without installer requirement changes: E-DES-01 now cites STATE/COMPOSE owners for02/04; ordinary rejection is E-DES-05 owned01. E-DES-04 covers clean/idempotent02/05, with dry-run split into E-DES-06 owned03. All six example requirement sets are subsets of every cited boundary owner set under PBF-R024; structural overlap-only success was not treated as semantic proof.
